first_impression.reaction: I went straight to the FAQ, like I always do, and the answers were short and actually pointed at sources: 'As at November 2026, Smartraveller puts it at November to April in Fiji and November to May in Mauritius.' Dates and a named source. That's what kept me here. The opening line 'November is a month of edges' is a bit of copywriter fluff, but the second paragraph names Smartraveller and the National Weather Service straight away, so I kept going. No 'the best', no 'award-winning'. Good start.

journey.quote: For couples weighing wedding destinations, November is a month of edges.
journey.reaction: Means nothing. Just tell me it's a month of trade-offs, which is what the rest of the page says anyway.
Good. No fake 'top 10' with a sponsored number one. I believe this more than a ranked list.

journey.section: How we chose these ten November destinations
journey.quote: We plan weddings in all ten, and each one has a live guide on this site.
journey.reaction: So the selection criterion is 'places we sell'. At least it's said out loud, which I respect. But it also tells me this list is a funnel, so I'll be checking whether the weather numbers lean optimistic. They don't, as it turns out.

journey.section: How we chose these ten November destinations
journey.quote: Base periods and the way a rain day is counted differ from country to country, and the WMO asks for care when city climates are set side by side, so read each figure on its own.
journey.reaction: This is the line that won me. Someone actually understood the data rather than lining up numbers that aren't comparable. Very few wedding sites would bother.

journey.quote: The page sets no threshold for a rain day, and November tops its rainfall column.
journey.reaction: They're telling me the Amalfi Coast is at its wettest in November, on a page that's trying to sell Amalfi weddings. That's honest about limitations. Checkable too.

journey.quote: IPMA counts any day with 0.1 mm or more, so a damp morning qualifies. These are older city normals, not a reading for Sintra.
journey.reaction: Caveats on the method and the station location. This is the sort of thing I'd go and verify, and I suspect it would hold up.

journey.quote: The Earth Sciences New Zealand climate summary for November 2025 describes one year, not a long-term normal.
journey.reaction: Appreciate them flagging it, but why is New Zealand, the 'plain spring choice', the one place without a long-term normal? One record-warm year tells me nothing about my date.

journey.quote: Will the resort put its wet weather and cyclone plans for the wedding in writing before we sign?
journey.reaction: The 'Questions for the venue' lists are the most useful bit of the page. Those are the questions I'd have written in my spreadsheet. Makes it feel like they're on the buyer's side.

journey.section: Wet and cyclone seasons in November
journey.quote: In the tropics, the rain plan belongs in the contract.
journey.reaction: Yes. Practical, contractual, not 'pray for sunshine'. Exactly the kind of thing my bad vendor experience taught me.

journey.quote: A Wedded Advisor works in your time zone, quotes in AUD and confirms each venue's inclusions in writing before you commit.
journey.reaction: Confirming inclusions in writing is good. But quoting in AUD on whose prices? The venue's, or the venue's plus your margin? This is where my real question starts and the page goes quiet.

journey.section: Plan your November wedding with Wedded Concierge
journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor is your single point of contact for the venue, travel, vendors and payments, anywhere in the world, and the fee is agreed in writing before any work begins.
journey.reaction: 'The fee is agreed in writing' is better than nothing, but it doesn't tell me what the fee is, how it's worked out, or whether you take a cut from the venue. And 'payments' running through you makes me want to know that even more. What's the catch?

unanswered_questions: How is the planner fee calculated (flat, percentage, tiered), and roughly what does it cost? The page says only that it is agreed in writing.
Do you take a commission or mark-up from venues or suppliers, and if so is it disclosed on the quote?
If payments go through the Wedded Advisor, are supplier prices passed on at cost, and can I see the supplier's own invoice?
What exactly does the fee include versus what costs extra?
Is there a long-term climate normal for New Zealand in November, rather than a single year's summary?
Can you show a real November wedding in any of these ten places with the actual budget?
What happens to your fee if a cyclone or venue closure forces a date change?

turn_offs_found.quote: For couples weighing wedding destinations, November is a month of edges.
turn_offs_found.why: Mood line instead of a fact. Minor, but it's the first sentence and it reads like marketing.

turn_offs_found.quote: Your Wedded Advisor is your single point of contact for the venue, travel, vendors and payments, anywhere in the world, and the fee is agreed in writing before any work begins.
turn_offs_found.why: Mentions a fee and handling payments without any fee model or supplier pricing transparency. That's precisely where I suspect the catch is hiding.

would_share_with: My partner, as a solid weather and trade-off comparison
A Reddit thread asking about November destination weddings, for the venue question lists

cta_reaction.quote: Tell us your November date, your guest numbers and who will need extra care on the journey through Wedded Concierge.
cta_reaction.why: The content earned enough trust that I'd consider it, and the CTAs come after the evidence, not before, which I like. But I'm comparing three planners and I enquire only once my main questions are answered. The fee model and whether you take a cut from venues aren't answered, so I'd probably go and look for a pricing or how-we-charge page first. If I can't find one, I'd enquire just to ask that one question, and I'd be blunt about it.

top_3_changes: OLD: "For couples weighing wedding destinations, November is a month of edges." NEW: "For couples weighing wedding destinations, November is a month of trade-offs." (Plain fact over mood. The rest of the page is built on the word trade-off anyway.)

OLD: "and the fee is agreed in writing before any work begins." NEW: "and the fee is agreed in writing before any work begins. Ask how that fee is worked out and how supplier prices are quoted to you, and get both answers in writing before you sign." (Adds no business facts, but signals you're not afraid of the question I'm going to ask anyway. Ideally link to a real fee page if one exists.)

OLD: "Ask each venue first, and get the answer in writing, with which rooms are heated and whether the full team works on your date." NEW: "It varies from venue to venue, so ask each one first, and get the answer in writing, with which rooms are heated and whether the full team works on your date." (The FAQ answer currently dodges the question. This gives the honest short answer, using the page's own line that opening and staffing vary from venue to venue.)

open_questions.question: Does Wedded Wonderland have a published fee model or commission disclosure page this post could link to near the closing CTA? Without it, the sceptic's likelihood to enquire stays at 3.
